reading_note: The teaching draws the contrast between two states: the eternal state, in which divine good and truth abide unchanged from the beginning in stillness — beyond what any merely natural mind can bring forth or disclose — and the state of death, the realm of self and matter where beginnings and endings, change and succession, hold sway. The arc moves from a meditation on the unchanging existence of light, through the impossibility of any natural man revealing what belongs to eternity, to the recognition that the realm of death has its own limited nature and substance, distinct from and bounded by the eternal stillness which precedes it.
